about: A text editor that runs in the terminal but works like a desktop one, shipped as one file with no setup.

prs.title: Unchanged Windows-style files no longer show as edited
prs.broken: Files saved with Windows line endings showed every line as changed in the editor's margin, even when nothing was touched. Other files showed a removed line at the end.
prs.changed: The margin now reads the saved version the same way the editor reads the file.
prs.matters: The change markers point only at lines you really changed.

prs.title: Replace in Files no longer loses unsaved or newer work
prs.broken: Replace in Files wrote to the saved file at positions found during the search. It threw away unsaved edits in an open tab, and garbled text that had changed since the search.
prs.changed: The editor now refuses files with unsaved edits, checks each match is still where it was, and names any file it skipped.
prs.matters: A project-wide replace never destroys work, and the count it reports is the real one.

prs.title: Ignored files stay hidden in folders with accented names
prs.broken: The editor hides or dims files that git is told to ignore. If the project sat in a folder with an accented or non-English name, it lost track of them, so clutter like build output showed up.
prs.changed: The editor now asks git in a way that returns names exactly as written, without git's special quoting.
prs.matters: Projects behave the same whatever language the folder names are in.

prs.title: Throwing away one file's changes no longer hits another
prs.broken: In web projects, folders are often named with brackets. Discarding changes to such a file also quietly undid edits in a different file whose name happened to match the pattern, losing work without warning.
prs.changed: The editor now tells git to treat each file name exactly as written, as it already did elsewhere.
prs.matters: Discard and stage touch only the file you picked, so no one loses work they meant to keep.

prs.title: The line's author is right even before you save
prs.broken: The editor shows who last changed the line you are on. After adding or removing lines without saving, it looked at the wrong line in the saved file and named the wrong person.
prs.changed: With unsaved changes, the editor now hands its current text to git, which matches each line to its real author.
prs.matters: The name you see is the person who actually wrote that line.

prs.title: Copied GitHub links open the right file again
prs.broken: The editor copies a GitHub link to your current line. With a space or # in the file name, a folder opened through a shortcut, or some remote styles, the link broke, and one kept your password.
prs.changed: The link is now built from the real file path, with each part of the name safely escaped, and the password and odd parts of the address are dropped.
prs.matters: The link you paste for a teammate opens the line you meant, and never leaks your login.
